problem: Collision-free robot paths can still disrupt ongoing human activities or violate social norms. Prior VLM-based social navigation works at a symbolic level (scoring abstract actions, group clustering, goal choice), ignore real execution effects and long-horizon planning, and large VLMs are too slow for real time.
motivation: Social etiquette (not crossing a photographer's line of sight, not cutting a queue, keeping away from a person on a ladder) needs semantic reasoning, but robot social-navigation data are scarce and social costs are hard to hand-design. Separating geometric feasibility from semantic judgment lets a VLM act as a proxy for the average human over concrete candidate paths.
key_idea: Sample diverse geometrically feasible, human-prediction-aware candidate paths, project them onto the camera image, and have a small VLM (Qwen-2.5 7B distilled from GPT-4o) pick the socially best path as a reference for an ORCA-based reactive controller.
insight: Splitting geometry (A* with anchors on a prediction-fused costmap) from semantics (VLM multiple-choice) gives collision-free and socially compliant paths, which direct VLM path generation does not: the appendix shows VLM-generated paths are mostly straight lines toward the goal. Longer human-motion prediction horizons reduce socially inappropriate candidates (group interruption falls from 39.17% at 0 s to 8.89% at 2.4 s), giving a cleaner candidate set. Selecting over full paths, rather than one-step actions, avoids the stuck or blocking behavior of VLM-Social-Nav, and the ablation shows that single-step selection largely reproduces VLM-Social-Nav's decisions.
method: Human Motion Extraction: YOLOv10 detection and ByteTrack tracking (40-frame buffer) on RGB. LiDAR points are projected to the image, and KMeans (3 clusters) inside each box gives the 3D position. Dynamic and pseudo-static states are distinguished, with velocity-constrained smoothing.

Prediction-Fused Costmap: LiDAR obstacle occupancy is overlaid with predictions from a neuralized-MRF stochastic trajectory predictor (2.4 s, 20 samples, ego-robot added as a graph node). Predictions get temporal decay weights 0.8 to 0.1, are aggregated by bin counting, and smoothed with a Gaussian filter.

Anchor-based Path Planning: A* is run start to anchor and anchor to goal. Anchors come from Poisson-disk-like grid sampling in a rectangle toward the goal. Hausdorff-distance clustering keeps 3-6 diverse paths, which are replanned continuously and projected onto the RGB image.

Social-compliance Selection: A VLM receives the image with numbered paths and outputs a structured answer (one-sentence description per path, chosen path, reason). GPT-4o gets richer prompts plus depth; Qwen gets a simplified RGB-only prompt.

Distillation fine-tuning: GPT-4o labels SCAND frames (goal 13-14.5 m away, path planner run on Velodyne obstacle maps, 1 Hz, human frames only), giving 4,851 train and 574 val pairs. Full SFT of Qwen-2.5 7B on 2 H100s, served with vLLM in 4-bit on a remote server.

Local reactive controller: Modified ORCA with a velocity-guided asymmetric responsibility (robot takes more responsibility as the pedestrian approaches along the line joining the two agents). The VLM-selected path is retrieved from the current candidates and its waypoints serve as sub-goals, decoupling VLM latency from control.

setting.backbone: Qwen-2.5 7B VLM (fully fine-tuned, 4-bit) for path selection; GPT-4o used as teacher/labeler; YOLOv10 + ByteTrack; neuralized-MRF trajectory predictor; A* + modified ORCA
setting.training_data: 4,851 image-selection pairs (574 val) from the SCAND dataset, labeled by GPT-4o
setting.observation: monocular RGB (fisheye) + 3D LiDAR point cloud + odometry
setting.action_space: selected path among 3-6 candidates as reference; ORCA velocity commands on a legged robot
setting.privileged: none (GT positions and group annotations only in the prediction-horizon ablation)

numbers_note: Only real-robot results on 4 custom scenarios (3 trials each); no standard benchmark. Fig. 6 social-ratio results are figure-only.
results: Across four real-world Spot scenarios, the method has zero social-zone intrusion time (SIT 0.00, Max SIR 0%) in all scenarios and the lowest PSV in three of four (0.00 in three, 0.33 in Queuing, where VLM-Social-Nav gets 0.00), against G-MPC, AttnGraph-RL, ViNT, VLM-Social-Nav and GSON. Baselines often fail to reach the goal within 90 s or intrude into social zones; GSON is the strongest baseline in group scenes but reacts late in dynamic ones.
limitations: No memory: the VLM sees only the current frame, missing context beyond the camera view (e.g., long queues)
Confounding or ambiguous simultaneous activities can confuse the VLM's prioritization of norms

Post-processing may exclude the ideal path, causing minimal clearance or overly conservative detours; VLM runs on a remote H100 server, and evaluation is on only 4 controlled scenarios with 3 trials each
